text:
maya_sales: Quick ask - new enterprise prospect (payments infra) requesting Private Deploy POC in 2 weeks. Requirements: PrivateLink for isolation, cross-AZ HA, on-prem fallback via TGW/BGP, and monthly EIP rotation for their compliance team. They also insist on seeing client src IPs in our auth logs. Need a concise netops handoff + a security checklist to paste into their ticket.

ran_neteng: Short answer: PrivateLink interface endpoints NAT to the ENI so original client IP is not preserved by default. Options to surface client identity: 1) run an in-VPC egress proxy that appends X-Forwarded-For (or a custom header) to requests; 2) use PROXY protocol between their proxy and our edge so we see the real IP; 3) route via TGW and have a customer-side NAT with stable EIP (if BYOIP allowed) so logs show that EIP. Each option affects TLS inspection and latency.

viv_arch: Infra notes: For AZ HA create interface endpoints in each AZ and front them with an HA proxy group (small autoscale). For cross-region either replicate VPCEs or use inter-region TGW. BGP failover pattern: prefer local VPCE routes, configure TGW BGP as secondary with a higher administrative distance. I can paste a sample BGP policy if needed.

harper_security: Security checklist (2 lines):
- Provide KMS policy snapshot for audit logs, confirm TLS mode (mTLS preferred) and cert rotation cadence.
- Agree to an EIP rotation schedule (we recommend monthly with a 2-hour maintenance window) and provide automation for firewall updates or accept FQDN allowlist.

ran_neteng: Minimal firewall snippet for their ops (replace placeholders):
```
# allow egress from customer VPC to Redwood POC
allow tcp from 10.100.0.0/16 to 18.200.45.99/32 port 443
# if using interface endpoints, allow to vpce ENIs or VPCE ID
allow tcp from 10.100.0.0/16 to vpce-0abc123def4567890 port 443
# healthchecks from our probe CIDR
allow tcp from 10.100.0.0/16 <- 15.200.100.0/24 port 443
```
Note: if they inspect TLS and rewrite SNI, recommend mTLS or PROXY protocol to avoid cert issues.

viv_arch: Cost guidance: PrivateLink has per-endpoint hourly + per-GB processing. Peering/TGW avoids per-endpoint fees but may have transit costs and more ops overhead. For a short POC (<1TB/mo) PrivateLink is simplest; for sustained multi-TB egress consider TGW/peering or Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity. Share estimated egress GB and peak RPS and Ill model numbers.

maya_sales: Can someone paste a 3-line network handoff and the 2-line security checklist I can put into the customer's ticket? They want kick-off in 10 business days.

harper_security: 2-line security checklist (ready to paste):
- Provide KMS key policy and required retention for audit logs; confirm TLS expectations (mTLS preferred) and certificate rotation cadence.
- Confirm monthly EIP rotation schedule and maintenance window; provide automation to update firewall rules or accept DNS/FQDN-based allowlist.

ran_neteng: 3-line netops handoff (ready to paste):
- Deploy PrivateLink interface endpoints in each AZ and front them with HA proxies for low-latency; enable PrivateLink DNS for service FQDN resolution.
- PrivateLink NATs client IP; to preserve original src IP use an in-VPC egress proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For, use PROXY protocol, or route via TGW with a customer NAT/BYOIP (if available).
- Open outbound TCP/443 to assigned EIP(s) or VPCE IDs; rotating EIPs monthly requires a maintenance window and automation to update firewall rules. Expect per-endpoint hourly + per-GB processing charges.
